whoWeAre.label: Who We Are
whoWeAre.title: A Professional Consulting Practice for International Business
whoWeAre.intro1: Nordic Riser AB is an international consulting firm specialising in strategic business establishment and structured professional relocation in Europe. We work with entrepreneurs, independent professionals, and business owners who are building a credible, legally compliant presence in European markets.
whoWeAre.intro2: Our work is advisory in nature. We do not provide legal representation or immigration services. Instead, we offer structured strategic guidance — combined with coordination of qualified professionals across legal, accounting, and regulatory disciplines — to ensure that every process our clients undertake is built on solid, defensible foundations.
whoWeAre.mission: “To provide strategic consulting services that help international entrepreneurs establish legally structured and sustainable business operations in Europe.”

whyWeExist.label: Why We Were Created
whyWeExist.title: Built to Address a Genuine Gap in International Advisory
whyWeExist.sub: We recognised that too many internationally minded professionals were navigating complex European business and relocation processes without access to structured, professional-grade strategic support.
problemParagraphs: International entrepreneurs and professionals often encounter fragmented advice — generic information that fails to account for their specific business model, professional background, or long-term objectives. The result is poor planning, avoidable delays, and structures that do not withstand institutional scrutiny.

Nordic Riser AB was established to change this. We bring a consulting firm's rigour to what is often an unstructured process — delivering clarity, documentation, and professional coordination at every stage.
Our focus is always on long-term strategy and sustainable outcomes, not short-term convenience.

s1.title: Introduction
body: Nordic Riser AB (“we”, “our”, or “us”) is committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring the security of your personal information. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you visit our website or engage with our advisory services.

This policy is designed to comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable data protection legislation. By using our website or submitting an inquiry, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this policy.

s2.title: Data Controller
body: Nordic Riser AB is the data controller responsible for your personal information collected through our website and services.
Nordic Riser AB — Email: info@nordicriser.com — Website: www.nordicriser.com
For all data protection matters, please contact us using the details above with the subject line “Data Protection Inquiry”.

subheadings.title: 3.1 Information You Provide Directly
subheadings.intro: We collect information that you voluntarily provide to us, including:
list: Contact Information: Name, email address, phone number
Professional Information: Business type, professional background, business objectives
Consultation Request Data: Purpose of consultation and description of your situation as submitted via our contact form
Communication Data: Information contained in emails and other correspondence with our team

subheadings.title: 3.2 Information Collected Automatically
subheadings.intro: When you visit our website, we may automatically collect:
list: Technical Data: IP address, browser type, operating system, device information
Usage Data: Pages visited, time spent on pages, navigation paths
Cookies: Small data files stored on your device (see Section 9)

s4.title: How We Use Your Information
s4.intro: We process your personal data only for the purposes outlined below, each supported by a lawful basis under GDPR:

rows: Responding to consultation requests and inquiries
Providing strategic advisory, technology, and global collaboration services
Communicating about our services and engagement progress
Improving our website and service quality
Compliance with legal and regulatory obligations

s4.note: We will not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties. We will not use your data for purposes incompatible with those stated above.

subheadings.title: 5.1 Professional Service Partners
subheadings.intro: Where required to deliver our services, we may share relevant information with qualified third-party professionals, including:
list: Legal counsel and specialist advisors engaged in connection with your matter
Accounting and tax professionals involved in business formation or compliance
Technology providers supporting our website hosting and communications infrastructure
subheadings.outro: All third parties are required to maintain appropriate security measures and are permitted to process your data only as directed by us and within the scope of their professional obligations.

subheadings.title: 5.2 Legal Requirements
subheadings.intro: We may disclose your personal information when required to do so by law, regulation, legal process, or a legitimate governmental request.

subheadings.title: 5.3 International Data Transfers
subheadings.intro: We primarily process data within the EU/EEA. In the event that data is transferred outside the EU/EEA, we ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place — such as Standard Contractual Clauses or applicable adequacy decisions — prior to any such transfer.

s6.title: Data Security
s6.intro: We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect your personal information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. These measures include:
list: Encrypted communication channels for the transmission of sensitive information
Secure server infrastructure and data storage systems
Access controls and authentication procedures for internal systems
Regular review and updating of security practices
Staff awareness of data protection obligations
s6.outro: While we take all reasonable precautions, no method of electronic transmission or storage is entirely secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security, but we are committed to protecting your data to the highest practicable standard.

s7.title: Data Retention
s7.intro: We retain your personal information only for as long as is necessary to fulfil the purposes outlined in this policy and to comply with our legal obligations:
list: Active Client Data: Duration of the engagement plus 7 years (in accordance with applicable accounting and record-keeping legislation)
Inquiry Data (non-converted): 2 years from the date of last contact
Website Analytics Data: Maximum 26 months
Consent Records: Until consent is withdrawn, plus a reasonable period thereafter for record-keeping purposes
s7.outro: Upon expiry of the applicable retention period, personal data is securely deleted or anonymised.

s8.title: Your Rights Under GDPR
s8.intro: As a data subject under the GDPR, you have the following rights in relation to your personal data:

rights.title: Right of Access
rights.body: Request a copy of the personal data we hold about you.

rights.title: Right to Rectification
rights.body: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data.

rights.title: Right to Erasure
rights.body: Request deletion of your data in certain circumstances (“right to be forgotten”).

rights.title: Right to Restrict Processing
rights.body: Request that we limit how we use your data in specified circumstances.

rights.title: Right to Data Portability
rights.body: Receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format where applicable.

rights.title: Right to Object
rights.body: Object to processing based on legitimate interests or for direct marketing purposes.

rights.title: Right to Withdraw Consent
rights.body: Withdraw any consent given at any time, without affecting prior processing.

rights.title: Right to Complain
rights.body: Lodge a complaint with the relevant supervisory authority (see Section 12).

s8.outro: To exercise any of the above rights, please contact us at info@nordicriser.com with the subject line “Data Subject Request”. We will respond within one calendar month as required by GDPR.

s9.title: Cookies and Tracking Technologies
body: Our website is a static informational site with minimal tracking. We may use essential cookies required for the basic operation of the site, including remembering your selected language. We do not currently use third-party advertising or behavioural tracking cookies.

If we implement analytics or additional tracking technologies in the future, we will obtain your prior consent before setting any non-essential cookies, provide clear information about each cookie's purpose and duration, and offer straightforward mechanisms to manage or withdraw your cookie preferences.
You may control and delete cookies through your browser settings at any time. Please note that disabling certain cookies may affect the functionality of the website.

s10.title: Children's Privacy
body: Our services are directed exclusively at adults conducting professional and business activities. We do not knowingly collect personal data from individuals under the age of 18. If you believe we have inadvertently collected data from a minor, please contact us immediately and we will take appropriate steps to delete that information.

s11.title: Changes to This Privacy Policy

list: Updating the “Last Updated” date at the top of this page
Where appropriate, notifying active clients by email
Posting a notice on our website
s11.outro: We encourage you to review this policy periodically. Your continued use of our website following any update constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

hero.label: Consulting
hero.h1: Strategic Consulting for International Business Establishment
hero.body: We provide structured, professional advisory across five core service areas — each designed to support entrepreneurs and professionals building a compliant business presence in Europe.

consulting.servicesSub: Every service we provide is delivered through a structured consulting methodology — assessed individually, documented formally, and coordinated with qualified professional partners where required.

services.title: Business Relocation Strategy Consulting
body: For entrepreneurs and professionals who intend to relocate to Europe through a structured business activity, this service provides strategic planning that begins with your business situation and works forward through the requirements of a legally compliant and institutionally defensible relocation process.

We assess your professional background, business model, and objectives, and develop a documented relocation strategy that integrates business structure, activity requirements, and long-term positioning. Our role is to ensure that every element of your plan is coherent, realistic, and aligned with regulatory frameworks — before any steps are taken.
We do not provide immigration advice or legal representation. We provide the strategic consulting framework from which qualified specialists can operate effectively.

services.title: Company Formation Strategy
body: Establishing a business entity in Europe requires careful strategic planning before any formal steps are taken. The choice of legal structure, jurisdictional considerations, ownership arrangements, and operational setup all have long-term implications — and errors at this stage are difficult and costly to correct.

This service provides structured consulting on how to approach company formation strategically. We help you understand the landscape of available structures, evaluate the most appropriate option for your situation, and develop a formation plan that supports both your immediate operational needs and your long-term business objectives.
Execution is coordinated with qualified legal and accounting professionals who handle the formal registration and compliance work within their licensed capacity.

services.title: Professional Business Plan Preparation
body: A business plan prepared for relocation or business establishment purposes is a formal document that must meet the expectations of European regulatory authorities, financial institutions, and professional reviewers. It is not a marketing document — it is a structured, evidence-based presentation of a viable business model.

We work with clients to develop business plans that accurately represent their activity, demonstrate operational viability, and are structured in line with institutional requirements. The process is methodical: we assess your business model, identify the documentation requirements relevant to your situation, and produce a plan that is coherent, credible, and professionally presented.

All business plans prepared through this service are developed to support formal processes — they are not generic templates, and they are not produced without a full understanding of the client's specific circumstances.

services.title: Freelancer & Entrepreneur Relocation Consulting
body: Independent professionals, remote workers, and small business owners face a distinct set of challenges when planning to establish a legal business presence in Europe. Standard frameworks are often designed with larger entities in mind, and the pathway for a sole trader or micro-business requires a more tailored strategic approach.

This service is specifically designed for freelancers, remote professionals, and early-stage entrepreneurs who are building — or planning to build — a legal and sustainable business base in Europe. We help you understand what a compliant structure looks like for your professional profile, what documentation and planning is required, and how to position your activity credibly within regulatory frameworks.

We assess each client individually. What is appropriate for a software consultant differs significantly from what is appropriate for a creative professional or a product-based entrepreneur — and our advisory reflects that.

services.title: Cross-Border Business Advisory
body: Entrepreneurs who operate across multiple countries face a more complex set of strategic and structural considerations. Questions of where to incorporate, how to manage cross-border transactions, how to structure ownership, and how to remain compliant across jurisdictions require careful and informed analysis — not generic answers.

This service provides advisory for internationally active business owners who need to think coherently about their multi-jurisdictional footprint. We help you map the relevant considerations, identify potential structural conflicts or opportunities, and develop a framework for managing your cross-border business activities in a way that is both operationally practical and compliant.
Where legal, tax, or regulatory specialist input is required — as it often is in cross-border matters — we coordinate engagement with qualified professionals in the relevant jurisdictions.

whoThisIsFor.label: Our Client Profile
whoThisIsFor.title: We Work With Four Distinct Client Groups
whoThisIsFor.sub: Our services are designed for professionals who require structured, compliance-grounded consulting — and who understand that building a business presence in Europe is a process that requires planning, documentation, and professional coordination.

groups.title: Entrepreneurs Planning to Relocate to Europe
body: This group consists of business founders and owner-operators who have decided — or are seriously considering — relocating to Europe through a structured business pathway. They typically have an existing business model or professional activity, and they understand that a credible, institutionally sound relocation strategy must be built on a properly established business foundation.
The challenge for most entrepreneurs in this group is not ambition — it is structure. Our role is to build that structure with them.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Developing a business plan that meets institutional standards for relocation processes
Selecting the most appropriate legal entity and business structure for their situation
Understanding the regulatory and compliance framework relevant to their business activity
Coordinating legal, accounting, and documentation requirements in a structured sequence
Building a long-term operational strategy for their European business presence

groups.title: Freelancers Working Internationally
body: Independent professionals — consultants, designers, developers, writers, and other knowledge-economy workers — increasingly operate across borders. Many in this group generate consistent professional income and work with international clients, but operate without the legal business structure that a European presence requires.

We work with freelancers to formalise their professional activity into a structured business framework — one that accurately reflects how they work and meets the expectations of European regulatory frameworks.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Translating freelance activity into a formally structured, documentable business model
Understanding which legal structure is appropriate for a sole trader or micro-business
Preparing professional documentation that demonstrates viable and consistent business activity
Planning a compliant and sustainable path to establishing a legal business base in Europe
Coordinating with relevant legal and accounting professionals for formal registration steps

groups.title: International Professionals
body: This group includes senior professionals, executives, and specialists who are planning to establish long-term business operations in Europe — either as a continuation of their existing professional career or as the foundation for a new phase of their working life.
What they require is a structured consulting framework that translates their professional background into a viable and compliant European business model.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Structuring professional experience and credentials into a formally viable European business model
Planning a corporate structure suited to long-term professional operations in Europe
Navigating cross-border compliance considerations relevant to their professional activity
Coordinating the documentation and planning required for a structured professional relocation
Establishing a business presence that positions them credibly within their professional sector

groups.title: Small Business Owners Expanding to European Markets
body: Small and medium-sized business owners seeking to expand their operations into European markets face a set of strategic and structural challenges distinct from those of a startup or sole trader.

We help small business owners think through their European expansion strategically — assessing the right entry approach, structuring the legal and operational framework, and coordinating the professional support required.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Developing a structured European market entry strategy suited to their business model
Selecting and designing the appropriate legal entity for European operations
Integrating a new European structure with their existing business operations and ownership
Managing cross-border compliance and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions
Coordinating legal, tax, and accounting professionals across the formation and setup process
